evidence: The dependency-neutral ObjectStore port accepts a binary stream and returns detached metadata or a controlled verified stream; neither the store nor stream exposes a filesystem path, raw SQLite connection, file name, or file descriptor.

Plaintext SHA-256 is immutable identity inside one project. The local adapter derives a different HMAC-SHA-256 physical name for each project, streams to an exclusive operation-scoped file, fsyncs, verifies stable single-link identity and exact bytes, then uses create-if-absent write-through publication before committing metadata.

Six concurrent identical puts and a restart produce one physical file and one metadata row. The same bytes in a second project retain the plaintext identity but use a different physical name; cross-project deduplication and equality exposure are absent.

Source interruption, caller hash mismatch, and invalid metadata leave no object row, published object, or partial staging file. Duplicate content with conflicting immutable metadata is rejected without changing the prior bytes or projection.

Open verifies full length/digest/identity before returning the held reader. On Windows, attempted write and unlink while that reader is live are denied. Missing, modified, or hardlinked content returns RO-CORE-OBJECT-CORRUPT before a byte is exposed and advances metadata to quarantined.

Reference counts are derived from immutable document revisions rather than a mutable counter. Two revisions referencing one object yield count 2 and deny deletion. Their repository transactions also produce two provenance and two outbox facts; an unreferenced byte put does not invent scholarly provenance.

Eleven direct tests cover success, concurrency, restart, rights, reference, corruption, hardlink, interruption, rollback, and controlled-stream boundaries. A forced SQLite failure after the object is moved for deletion rolls the file and metadata back exactly and exposes neither __cause__ nor __context__.

A hardlinked abandoned staging entry fails closed without mutating the outside alias. Denied and unknown rights states cannot be opened; allowed and not-applicable are the only readable states in the exact profile.

ADR-0015 and the strict Draft 2020-12 project-object-store-v1 profile bind content identity, project deduplication scope, opaque physical identity, atomic publication, canonical metadata/reference authority, rights, verified streaming, and the staged encryption handoff.

No SQLite migration is required: the approved version-2 object_records and immutable documents relations already provide the exact metadata and first reference authorities. T03 owns expansion of the reference graph rather than a premature schema counter.

The architecture guide explicitly marks plaintext-fixture-v1 as an intermediate unencrypted adapter that is not release-qualified. T02 must add authenticated streaming encryption/key metadata; T03 owns quotas, leases, garbage collection, cache eviction, and the slice performance benchmark.

The real frozen Core sidecar contains both the private adapter and dependency-neutral port, while architecture checks deny direct concrete-adapter imports outside the governed data/composition boundary. No UI or approved reference bytes changed.
